title: GridForge Spreadsheet - Harness Run QC
subtitle: Fairness audit of OpenHands gpt-5.6-sol xhigh run 07, reported reward 0.5556.
note: Scope: jobs/gridforge-gpt-5.6-sol-xhigh-07/gridforge-spreadsheet__WLvkjEk. Evidence was checked against reward-details.json, verifier logs, the captured model app source, the current instruction and rubric, and Oracle run 02.

runs.note: Oracle run 02 passed 20/20, but its task checksum differs from model run 07. The 20 criterion descriptions and weights are identical.
Valid graded run with no exception, timeout, action-error, or cascade. Passed weight 10.0 of 18.0.

tasks.name: GridForge Run 07
tasks.headline: The five reported failures are based on real model behavior, but the rubric contains one contradictory false pass, one under-specified security requirement, and duplicated formula weighting.

findings.what: forged_save_identity_and_stale_rejections passed even though its all-or-nothing checklist explicitly requires a valid-user/live-session mismatch to be rejected. The same run's api_session_user_mismatch_rejected criterion proved that this exact mismatch returned HTTP 200 and changed attribution.
findings.why: The batched browser judge exercised only a subset of the broader criterion, then generalized that all identity probes passed. Its own second verdict contradicts that conclusion.
findings.impact: The official reward is inflated. If the 2.0-weight forged-save criterion follows its written all-or-nothing rule, passed weight becomes 8.0 of 18.0 and the score is 0.4444, not 0.5556.
findings.fix: Remove the valid-user/session-mismatch leg from the broad forged-save criterion because it already has a dedicated criterion, or require an explicit per-probe result table and fail the broad criterion when that leg is accepted.
findings.evidence: CONFIRMED: forged_save_identity_and_stale_rejections reasoning cites only an unknown user and a stale-cell conflict, while api_session_user_mismatch_rejected records Riley's session accepting userId=morgan with HTTP 200. Captured server.js:104 and :144-153 trusts body.userId for revision attribution.

findings.what: The model genuinely permits one seeded user to submit a save attributed to another, but the criterion mandates authorization through the current live session ID even though the instruction never states that a collaboration session ID must authorize save requests.
findings.why: The instruction requires a seeded-user login, correct edit attribution, and a server trust boundary. Those support rejecting impersonation at the behavioral level, but they do not prescribe the verifier's exact live-session mechanism.
findings.impact: The observed model behavior is defective, so this is not a fabricated failure. However, a different correct implementation using a cookie or token rather than the collaboration session ID could be judged against an implementation detail it was never told to expose.
findings.fix: State that the server must bind every save to the authenticated signed-in user and reject a payload that claims another user, while allowing any secure session or token mechanism.
findings.evidence: PARTIAL: captured client app.js:18 sends client-controlled userId and no authorization credential; server.js:104 only checks that the user exists and then attributes revisions to body.userId. The behavioral failure is confirmed, while the required session-ID mechanism is under-specified.

findings.what: formula_bar_raw_formula_and_precedence and formula_reference_replacement_selection both failed because the same autocomplete overlay intercepted B2. Together they remove 3.5 of 18.0 weight for one root defect.
findings.why: The broad precedence criterion repeats the cell-reference click path that the dedicated replacement criterion already owns. Both are binary and all-or-nothing, so the overlay erases credit for unrelated precedence checks that the judge says passed.
findings.impact: Both verdicts are behaviorally fair, but the aggregate score overstates defect breadth. Crediting either one of the duplicated penalties would produce 0.6389 or 0.6667; the model still remains below the 0.7 target.
findings.fix: Keep reference clicking and replacement in the dedicated criterion; make the raw-formula criterion test raw preservation and precedence without repeating that gate, or account for both under one formula-authoring feature score.
findings.evidence: CONFIRMED: both failed reasonings name the same fixed-position suggestion list over B2. Captured app.js:24 positions suggestions below the formula bar, while instruction.md:115-116 requires the dropdown below the edited cell.

findings.what: range_functions_dependency_recalculation is a fair failure. Formula-mode mousedown returns before enabling drag extension, and the evaluator treats a standalone cell argument such as G22 as Number('G22'), which becomes zero.
findings.why: The implementation can evaluate and recalculate simple single ranges, but cannot build F22:F24 through the required mouse drag and drops G22 from SUM(F22:F24,G22).
findings.impact: The verifier catches two independent model defects. Even if multi-argument function syntax is viewed as an implicit spreadsheet convention, the explicitly stated grid range-reference interaction still fails and independently justifies a no verdict.
findings.fix: No rubric fix is required for the overall verdict. For cleaner diagnosis, split formula-range authoring from multi-argument calculation semantics.
findings.evidence: CONFIRMED: app.js:31 returns from formula-mode mousedown before state.drag=true; app.js:10 evaluates non-range function arguments with Number(part) rather than resolving cell references. Instruction.md:112-120 covers ranges, functions, and grid reference insertion.

findings.what: name_box_jump_and_range_selection is a fair failure. Entering T80 changes selection state but never scrolls the target into view.
findings.why: The model's jump() directly updates anchor and focus, renders, and broadcasts selection. It does not call select() or scrollIntoView(), even though ordinary selection does.
findings.impact: The named jump feature is unusable for off-screen addresses. The criterion costs only 0.5 and its other range, invalid-address, clear, and undo checks passed.
findings.fix: No verifier change is needed; keeping an off-screen address is the right positive test for actual navigation.
findings.evidence: CONFIRMED: the judge measured T80 around 2470px below a roughly 448px viewport with scrollTop still zero; source app.js:20 has no scrolling call. Instruction.md:61-62 explicitly requests name-box jumping.

findings.what: Several passing all-or-nothing criteria have reasoning that documents only a subset of their required actions. For example, workbook_load_custom_surface_status does not mention the exact B2/C2/D2 or A14/A40/A80 checks, and forged_save_identity_and_stale_rejections omits most identity probes and reaches a conclusion contradicted elsewhere.
findings.why: All 20 long criteria are judged in one batched agent session with no stored ATIF trajectory or screenshots. A concise final summary is the only surviving proof, so omitted sub-checks cannot be distinguished from unexecuted sub-checks.
findings.impact: This creates a false-pass risk and has already produced one confirmed false pass. The nominal 15/20 pass count should not be treated as proof that every conjunctive leg was exercised.
findings.fix: Split long criteria into feature/subfeature checks or require the judge to return one explicit pass/fail/evidence entry for every numbered probe before computing the criterion verdict.
findings.evidence: CONFIRMED by the missing evidence in reward-details.json and the direct contradiction documented in GF07-01. No screenshots or ATIF trajectory were retained for independent replay.

findings.what: Oracle run 02 scored 1.0 on 20/20 and its criterion text and weights match model run 07, but the Harbor task checksums differ: 96abc53a... for Oracle and 46711076... for the model.
findings.why: At least one task file changed between runs. The matching rubric proves the same browser criteria were used, but the checksum mismatch prevents claiming that the complete task snapshot was identical.
findings.impact: Solvability is strongly supported but not formally proven for the exact model-run artifact. This is a provenance gap, not evidence that any of the five model failures is false.
findings.fix: Freeze the task tree, rerun Oracle and the target model from that exact checksum, and record the checksum beside both results.
findings.evidence: PARTIAL: Oracle 02 has reward 1.0 and 20/20; a direct comparison found no criterion description or weight differences, but result.json records different task_checksum values.

blocks.title: Fairness Verdict
items: No failed criterion was caused by a timeout, action error, blank app, or cascade.
Formula overlay, formula-range drag/calculation, and name-box scrolling failures are clearly fair.
Session impersonation is a real model defect, but the exact live-session authorization mechanism needs one explicit instruction sentence.
The run contains a confirmed false pass, not a false failure: forged_save_identity_and_stale_rejections should also have failed.

blocks.title: Score Interpretation
items: Applying the broad forged-save criterion as written: 8.0 / 18.0 = 0.4444.
Giving back either duplicated formula penalty still leaves the model at or below 0.5556 after correcting the false pass, comfortably below the 0.7 target.

blocks.title: Run Health
items: The trial completed normally with graded=1, no_op=0, and no exception.
SQLite seed/restart idempotence passed before browser grading.
The only app stderr entry was the expected invalid-JSON probe; it did not crash the server.
